# BH00009 (Unnamed)

*Translated on 17 Qudrat 183 using GPT 6.1 Sol*

**1** In the name of our Lord, the Most Holy, the Most Great, the Most High, the Most Glorious.

**2** Today the rustling of the Tree beyond which there is no passing rises high, and the sun of utterance shines resplendent from the horizon of the heaven of meanings. The Path speaks with the most eloquent expression, and the Balance makes mention in the most perfect words. Yet the banner of “There is none in the realm but Him” is planted and raised aloft, for the world is lifeless and despondent—indeed, dead. There is no ear to listen and no eye to behold, except for a few whom the veils of names and the coverings of allusions and words did not hold back. They left behind all but the True One and joined themselves to Him. They heard the call, drank the choice wine, and arose for the Cause with such resolve that it caused the hearts of the aggressors to tremble and the feet of those who associate partners with God to falter. In truth, not every ear is fit to hear, nor are diseased eyes, lacking clear vision, capable of beholding. Today is the day of remembrance and praise. For whom? For the friends, those who stand firm in the Cause with perfect steadfastness and speak in remembrance of the Desire of the world. Every remembrance and every praise befits those assured souls, content with God and pleasing to Him.

**3** Glory be to You, O You in separation from whom those brought near have lamented, and at whose absence the sincere have cried out. I ask You, by the lights of the dawn of Your revelation, through which You have brought Your servants and Your creation to life and given those in every land the glad news of union with You and attainment to Your presence, to assist Your friends in that through which the manifestations of Your might and the evidences of Your power may be exalted. O Lord, adorn the records of the world and the books of the nations with their names. You indeed have power over whatever You will. There is no God but You, the Helper, the Bestower, the All-Powerful, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. O my God and the God of the world, my Desire and the Desire of the nations! I ask You, by Your sweetest call raised between earth and heaven, and by the radiance of the lights of Your face from the most exalted horizon, to protect whoever has arisen to serve Your Cause and spoken Your praise. Then strengthen him with the hosts of the unseen and the seen, and aid him with a company of angels and the Spirit. You are indeed the All-Powerful, whom neither the power of rulers nor their might, nor the doubts raised by the learned nor their insinuations, can thwart. There is no God but You, the All-Protecting, the All-Powerful, the Almighty, the Most Great.

**4** O beloved of my heart! I was looking, reflecting, grieving, and pondering the manifestations of our Lord’s power, what had befallen Him, and what had proceeded from the factions. Then the door opened, and the bearer of your letter entered—a letter from which everyone endowed with a sense of smell perceived the fragrance of your sincerity, your love, your turning toward God, our Lord and your Lord, and your resolve to serve the Cause in days when the might of the heedless had seized the inhabitants of the cities of names, except those whom God, the Lord of all and the Sovereign of the next world and this one, had protected. When I read it, I found in each of its letters that which acquainted me with what was in your hearts and made known to me what had drawn your heart, your very veins, your outward and inward being: the Cause of God, to whose cord you have held fast and to whose hem you have clung, to exalt His Word and guide His servants and His creation. When I understood this, I flew on the wings of longing toward God, the Lord of the Covenant. I entered His presence and presented it to the end. Then the gentle rustling of the Tree beyond which there is no passing arose, and the Lord of all spoke words that this servant cannot fittingly recount. I ask Him to sustain me through His grace and generosity. Can any writer number the waves of the sea as they appear and rise? No, by His own true Self, except through assistance from Him and grace from His presence. There is no God but Him, who records all things in a clear Book.

**5** And at the close of His utterances—may the souls of all in the kingdoms of command and creation be sacrificed for Him—He said, exalted be His utterance and glorious His proof:

**6** He is the Watchful, the Witness, the Knowing, the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.

**7** The Tree of Utterance at the pivot of the contingent world calls out: “There is no God but Me, the All-Protecting, the Self-Subsisting.” The Tree beyond which there is no passing, upon the luminous earth beyond the ocean of grandeur: “By God, the Hidden One has come with manifest sovereignty!” The Tree of Certitude, planted in the land of saffron, calls out: “The Sovereign has come! Sovereignty belongs to God, the Lord of existence.” The Tree of Proof upon the white spot declares: “The fragrance of the garment has spread, and the light has shone from the horizon of revelation. Hasten, people of the earth, and do not follow anyone who is ignorant and veiled.” This is a day on which the mountains have bowed down, for the Self-Sufficient, the Most Exalted, has come with the banner of power and the standard of “There is no God but Me, the Lord of the unseen and the seen.” Say: “People of Iran, fear the All-Merciful and do not be among those who do not know. We have blown the trumpet, which is My Most Exalted Pen, and through it We have brought to life those who were in My preserved knowledge.”

**8** Say: “People of the Bayān, have you heard and yet denied? Have you seen and yet turned away? Fear God and judge fairly concerning this Cause, at whose appearance souls were shaken, except those whom God took hold of, rescued from the darkness of vain imaginings, and raised to a station where they heard the call of the Kingdom.” O Warqāʾ, hear the call as you have heard it before and since.

**9** The servant attending here arrived with your letter. When he read it in the presence of the Wronged One, the Pen of your Lord, the Self-Subsisting, began to move and revealed for you that which made the mouth of utterance smile and stirred those in the graves. We have revealed for you that which is a light to the books of the world, a straight path for the followers of religions, and a mighty pillar for whoever acknowledges this momentous announcement. Say: “You who turn away, listen and then judge fairly. By the life of God, the call draws you to a station where you lay aside what you possess in the hope of what is with God, the Almighty, the All-Loving.” Say: “This is the arena of proof; bring forward what you have. By the life of God, none ride in it but the horsemen of certitude, who have cast the world aside and turned toward God, the Lord of the promised Day.” Thus has the sea brought forth the shells of wisdom and utterance, and the Tree its fruits, but the people do not know.

**10** Hear the call of the Wronged One in the Persian tongue. What was hidden has become manifest, and what had ever been stored in the heaven of the divine will and preserved in the Preserved Tablet has been sent down. Yet the recompense for their deeds deprived all of the outpourings of the Day of Return, just as the deeds and their recompense were seen among the people of the Qurʾān, particularly the Shiʿi community. O Warqāʾ, reflect on the lack of discernment of those deluded souls among the people of the Bayān. Although the veils were torn apart, and they saw with their outward eyes the conjectures, vain imaginings, unbelief, hypocrisy, oppression, and tyranny of the former community, they are now once again occupied in organizing a Shiʿi community; they wish to make a people into Shiʿis. In short, vain imaginings and names have deprived people of the ocean of meanings and denied them a share in true recognition of divine unity. In truth, in one respect names are idols, as has been and continues to be witnessed. Even now the former community has not taken heed or risen from the sleep of heedlessness. Each day the fire of oppression blazes more fiercely, and the flame of malice and hatred burns more brightly. Today it is necessary and incumbent upon all to arise to aid the Cause, which consists in protecting weak souls from conjectures and vain imaginings.

**11** Convey to the friends in that land, on behalf of the Wronged One, the greeting “God is Most Great.” Say: “Strive, that you may attain the lights of the sun of true recognition of divine unity. Whoever attains it will find himself free and released from the world.” Blessed are those who act, and blessed are those who recognize. May the glory manifest and shining from the horizon of the heaven of My Kingdom rest upon you and upon whoever listens to your words concerning the Cause of God, the Lord of the worlds. End.

**12** O beloved of my heart! The sun of the All-Merciful’s utterance shines with such radiance that all the utterance of the world, from the beginning of creation until now, bows in humility and reverence at its appearance and revelation. What, then, can this lost one submit, and what can he express? This mortal servant is bewildered by what those clamorous voices are saying and what they cling to. The worth and station of certain people are now becoming clear. Although all have seen with their outward eyes the audacity of the former community and witnessed the idolatry, heedlessness, hypocrisy, and oppression of those souls, they nevertheless speak now of a mirror, now of a successor, now of a deputy, a noble one, a chief, and the like. Glory be to God! They have denied whatever was previously revealed that runs counter to the desires of those who turn away. They have utterly denied the Persian Bayān, which is in truth among the greatest books of the Primal Point—may the soul of all besides Him be sacrificed for Him. They have said it has been altered. We must all lament and cry, “Alas!” The lies of the past have been resurrected, and the former fabrications have reappeared. We belong to God, and to Him we return.

**13** O beloved of my heart! The fair-minded and discerning know and recognize the greatness of the Revelation, its all-encompassing power, and likewise what has been sent down from the heaven of His will. They behold, as plainly as the sun, the lights of the revelation of the Lord of all. Nevertheless, this tribe of apish creatures, defiled, dust-covered, and filthy, are seen to resemble the divines of the Shiite community, who, in the corners of their seminaries, made a filthy show of asceticism and wickedly claimed knowledge and faith. They have never been, and are not now, worthy of this court. Praise be to God, who has sanctified His court from meeting them, His light from their sight, His Revelation from their recognition, and His call from their hearing. They have resorted to scheming, deceit, and trickery. Some deeds of those heedless, ignorant souls have been recounted that leave every rational person bewildered. May God protect us and you from the evil of these people.

**14** As to your remark that this servant’s correspondence has been infrequent, I fully acknowledge the truth of this statement, for I should send at every moment something fragrant with the loving care and compassion of our Beloved and yours, our Desired One and yours, and the Desired One of all in the heavens and on earth. Yet, O beloved of my heart, letters have arrived and continue to arrive from all quarters in such numbers that this servant has truly had, and still has, no opportunity to express to the friends what is in his heart. Two years have passed, and replies to some of the gentlemen—may God’s glory and loving care rest upon them—have been and remain overdue. I ask and hope that God, exalted be His glory, will grant assistance and success. He is powerful and mighty. Most of your letters, however, have been answered. The one God is my witness: whenever a letter from that beloved friend has arrived, it has brought fresh joy and delight. Besides this, for some time certain discussions have arisen in this land as well, and prudence must sometimes be observed.

**15** Above all, you know that day and night I am occupied in His presence with transcribing the divine verses. Yet that beloved friend also has a share and portion in this servant’s services. This statement is adorned with the testimony of the Desired One of the worlds. \[corrupted original text\] to you. You had also mentioned my beloved friend, Jinab-i Amin—may God’s glory and loving care rest upon him. He himself has written a letter to this servant. He has always mentioned you in all his letters. He has truly been, and remains, a well-wisher of the friends. I ask and hope that God will assist him in every circumstance. He is indeed the Compassionate; He is indeed the Generous.

**16** As to the glad news you conveyed that some of the friends of God have abandoned harmful habits, after this matter was presented at the most holy, most exalted threshold, He said: “We ask God, exalted be His glory, for the sanctification and purification of all. Today, good deeds and praiseworthy character are the hosts of God on earth, and through these hosts God has granted and continues to grant victory. O you who speak in My name, gaze toward My horizon, and soar in the atmosphere of My love! Repeatedly convey to the friends in that land, on behalf of this Wronged One, the greeting ‘God is Most Great.’ Each and every one is remembered in the presence of God, and their remembrance flows from the Most Exalted Pen.”

**17** “Convey the greeting ‘God is Most Great’ to Jinab-i Mim and Sad—may God’s glory rest upon him. We ask God to assist him in what befits His Day, and likewise in a deed whose fragrance will never cease. Praise be to God, he has attained the blessing of turning toward Him and has been adorned with the remembrance of the Most Exalted Pen.” End.

**18** This mortal one also beseeches God, exalted be His glory, to sanctify him from transitory concerns and adorn him with qualities that will exalt the Word of God. Spirits were created for this, bodies were brought into being for this, and the sun, the moon, and all things came into existence for this service. God willing, may he be enabled to remember and praise Him and to teach the Cause. I convey to him the greeting ‘God is Most Great’ and my salutations, and ask God to assist him.

**19** What you mentioned concerning Jinab-i Suhrab and his turning toward the Most Exalted Horizon attained the honor of being heard at the most holy, most exalted threshold. His words—exalted be His praise and mighty His proof: “O Suhrab! The Comforter has come to speak what has remained unspoken, to make heard what has remained unheard, and to bring to completion what has been said. Praise the Beloved of the worlds that you have turned toward the loftiest summit and the ultimate goal, which is recognition of God Himself, exalted be His glory. Rend the veils of vain imaginings and shatter the idols of conjecture, that you may be illumined by the rays of the Sun of truth and certitude and attain your goal. The loving Father came, but the children did not recognize Him and were deprived of recognizing Him, except for a few whom the doubts raised by patriarchs, metropolitans, bishops, and priests did not keep from the Dawning-Place of the light of divine unity. The call is raised, but a tongue that attains the word ‘Yes’ is nowhere to be found. Ask God to grant awareness and bestow understanding. He indeed has power over whatever He wills through His word ‘Be,’ and it is.” End.

**20** As to what you wrote concerning the spiritual friend, Jinab-i Ayn and Ba—may the glory of God, the All-Glorious, rest upon him—praise be to God, he has received the fragrant breezes of these days. He is mentioned in the divine Book and inscribed by the Most Exalted Pen in the Crimson Scroll. No favor can equal this favor, and every station bows before this station. I ask and hope that God, exalted be His glory and all-embracing His bounty, will assist him in preserving this most exalted station and lofty rank. May joy be his, may it bring him delight and satisfaction, and blessed be he! These matters were presented in the presence of the Lord of Revelation. This utterance appeared from the kingdom of the loving care of the Beloved of the worlds. His words—exalted be His grandeur and mighty His sovereignty:

**21** He is the Witness from His most exalted horizon.

**22** “We have remembered him with a remembrance that the happenings of the contingent world will not alter, nor the centuries and ages change; it will abide forever in the Book of God, the Lord of the worlds. By My life! There has been ordained for him that which the earth and its treasures cannot equal. To this the Mother Book bears witness in this palace, whose very atoms proclaim: ‘By God! He who spoke on Sinai has ascended the throne of Revelation,’ and the Tongue has declared: ‘Sovereignty and the heavenly kingdom, might and dominion, station and divinity belong to My own Self, the Almighty, the Ancient.’ We ask God to open before his face the doors of loving care and gracious favor, and to draw him near to Himself in every circumstance. He indeed has power over whatever He wills, and He is the Most Bountiful, the Generous. We have remembered him in another Tablet, that he may rejoice and be among the thankful. Thus has mercy revealed its showers, the Pen its mysteries, and the Sun of inner meanings its radiance. He is indeed the All-Powerful, the All-Forgiving, the Merciful. May the glory shining from the horizon of the heaven of My grace rest upon him and upon those who have believed in God, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.” End. The ocean of bounty bears witness to bounty, and its waves are evidence of it. The sun itself makes its own station clear, and its rays are its proof. What more, then, can this mortal servant mention or submit that would be fitting and worthy?

**23** You mentioned Jinab-i Khalil—may God’s glory rest upon him. Praise be to God, he has been and remains favored with success. He has been mentioned at the most holy, most exalted threshold. This mortal one asks God, exalted be His glory, to enable him to serve His Cause. He is indeed the Hearer, the Answerer. O beloved of my heart! Most of the writings of the Most Exalted Pen fell into the hands of the adversaries during the affair of Ta. Everyone who was arrested had books, scriptures, and Tablets with them. That beloved friend should alert the people of God, so that all may make strenuous efforts to preserve and honor the Tablets and writings, exerting themselves to the utmost. Blessed is the land in which the fragrance of the sound of the Most Exalted Pen is diffused. Preserving the exalted, unassailable, blessed Tablets is most necessary and is beloved in God’s sight, lest the pages and their written lines fail to retain their original form. Explain and teach the means of preserving them. What has been mentioned here is in accordance with the most holy, most exalted command. Blessed are those who act.

**24** You had mentioned Jinab-i Mirza Muhammad Husayn Kha Alif and Jinab-i Abbasquli Kha Alif—may God’s glory rest upon them both. After the matter was presented in His presence, two most holy, most exalted Tablets were revealed especially for them and dispatched. I ask God, exalted be His glory, that they may attain the lofty heaven within the Tablet and be illumined by the lights of its suns and moons, in such a way that the happenings of the days may not alter it, nor the oppression of the pharaohs of the age and the tyrants of the lands obscure it. This is not difficult for God, our Lord and your Lord.

**25** The words of the Lord, exalted and sanctified is He: “He is the Light shining from the horizon of the world.”

**26** This is a day on which the One sought calls out and brings humanity glad tidings of His irrevocable decree and His sealed wine. Blessed are those who have turned toward Him with radiant faces and luminous hearts, taken the cup of bounty from the hand of the Lord of Names and Creator of heaven, and drunk in His name, the All-Subduing, the Self-Subsisting. The fire has appeared from the Lote-Tree, and He who spoke on Sinai has spoken from the horizon of the heaven of revelation: “People of the earth! By God, the promise has come, and the Promised One, from His praiseworthy station, calls you to God, the Lord of the unseen and the seen.” The All-Merciful has revealed Himself to all who dwell in the realm of existence, and the Most Great Vision has appeared. The Lord of destiny says: “Humankind! Turn toward the all-glorious horizon, then listen to the sound of My Most Exalted Pen. It guides you to the path of God, the Lord of all that has been and all that will be.”

**27** You who have been mentioned before the Wronged One! We have heard you mentioned and have remembered you with that which nothing possessed by the nations, or by princes and kings, can equal. Blessed are you for having received the writings of My Most Exalted Pen and for having had your name spoken by the Wronged One as He sat upon the throne of His name, the All-Loving. We have sent down the verses, made the clear proofs manifest, and torn through the veils before all eyes, undeterred by the might of the world. To this bears witness the one who possesses an inscribed Book.

**28** Afflictions have surrounded Us on every side, and calamities from every quarter, while the Pen of the Chosen One has continued to proclaim, at dusk and at sunrise, in the early morning and in the evening: “There is no God but Me, the Truth, the Knower of all hidden things.” Blessed is the one who has heard My call, turned toward My horizon, voiced My praise, arisen to serve My Cause, and held fast to My outstretched cord. When the breezes of My verses draw you and the river of My utterance takes hold of you,

**29** Say: “My God, my God! You see the distant one seeking nearness to You, the poor one the ocean of Your riches, and the thirsty one the river of Your bounty. I ask You, by the lights of the sun of Your utterance, the mysteries of Your Book, Your most exalted horizon, and all that lies stored in the treasuries of Your Pen and the repositories of Your knowledge, O Lord of Names and Creator of heaven, to strengthen me to remain steadfast in Your Cause and arise to serve You. My Lord! You see me affirming what the Tongue of Your grandeur has spoken in the kingdom of Your utterance, and acknowledging what has descended from the heaven of Your will. Strengthen my heart and my limbs, my God, so that neither the might of the powerful nor the doubts raised by the learned may weaken them. Then set me ablaze with the fire of Your Lote-Tree and illumine me with the lights of Your throne. I ask You, O Ruler of the signs, by Your command through which You have raised the banners of Your revelation throughout the horizons and the standards of Your victory throughout the lands, to inscribe for me with the Pen of Your grace that which will remain with me in every world of Your worlds. You are indeed powerful to do whatever You will, and in Your grasp are the reins of all things. You do what You will and decree what You desire. There is no God but You, the Unique, the One, the All-Subduing, the Almighty, the All-Bountiful.” End.

**30** And this is what was revealed for Jinab-i Abbasquli Khan, may the glory of God rest upon him. The words of the Lord, exalted and sanctified is He:

**31** In My name, the All-Subduing over all names.

**32** At this moment the Lote-Tree of utterance, planted in the most exalted Paradise by the hand of divine providence, speaks these words: “People of the earth! Abandon your vain imaginings and conjectures. This is the day on which the seal of the sealed wine has been broken in the name of God, the All-Subduing, the Self-Subsisting. Come forward and drink from it, despite every heedless outcast and every veiled scholar.” Blessed is the soul who has heard its call and tasted the sweetness of its utterance. By the lights of the sun of meanings shining from the horizon of the heaven of utterance! Every soul who attains to hearing will be set ablaze with such a fire that neither the world’s rejection nor the nations’ objections will hinder or deprive that soul, and its effects will become plain and manifest. From the earliest days until now, without concealment or veil, We have called out before the faces of rulers, scholars, and jurists—a call to hear which ears have been brought from nonexistence into existence. Yet outward ornaments and fleeting colors have barred the servants from everlasting, eternal blessings and deprived them of these.

**33** When you hear the melodies of the birds of meaning upon the branches of utterance, cleanse your heart and breast with the water of turning toward God and detachment, and say:

**34** “My God, my God! Praise be to You for having made Your path manifest among Your servants and called humanity to the dawning-place of Your revelation, the dayspring of Your inspiration, and the source of Your commandments and laws. I testify that You have shown the way, sent down the proof, and commanded everyone to do what will draw them near to You and benefit them in every world of Your worlds. I ask You, O Lord of existence, by the waves of the ocean of Your generosity and the lights of the sun of Your grace, to sustain me in all circumstances, that I may speak Your remembrance, burn with the fire of Your love, be mindful of Your verses, soar in Your heaven, hold fast to the cord of Your bounty, and cling to the hem of Your generosity. My Lord! You see Your servant turning toward Your most exalted horizon, acknowledging Your oneness and uniqueness, and affirming Your grandeur and sovereignty. I ask You, by Him who hastened to the place of sacrifice out of longing to meet You and welcomed the arrows of affliction out of love for Your beauty, to grant me the blessing You have sent down from the heaven of Your Cause and the table You have sent from the kingdom of Your utterance. You are the One whom neither the ranks of the world nor its armies can hinder. You do what You will and decree what You desire. There is no God but You, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy. I further ask You, O Lord of eternity, by the Most Great Name through which You have illumined the world, to ordain for me the good of the next life and this life. You are indeed the Lord of Names and Creator of heaven. There is no God but You, the All-Powerful, the Almighty, the Ever-Bestowing.” End.

**35** Gracious care belongs to God; grace is His, and bounty is His. For every soul who is present in the most holy court or whose name is mentioned there, something has been revealed in each word of which oceans of grace and loving care lie concealed. Blessed is the eye that has attained it and the heart that has drunk from it. This servant conveys greetings and salutations to each of these honored friends and asks the everlasting God to strengthen them in service to His Cause, so that through His name they may conquer the cities of hearts. By His own Self, the Truth! The sword of utterance is sharper, and the influence of the Word is beyond reckoning. In every circumstance, as commanded, wisdom must be observed. This command takes precedence over most ordinances, for it has been revealed and issued by the Most Exalted Pen in numerous Tablets. Blessed are those who act accordingly.

**36** You wrote that Jinab-i Aqa Khalil Ha Ma—may the glory of God and His loving care rest upon him—had initially undertaken to convey the Word together with the two aforementioned souls. After this matter was presented in the most inaccessible, most holy court, a Tablet especially for him was revealed from the heaven of grace and dispatched. God willing, he will receive it and gain oceans upon oceans from the utterance of the Desire of all worlds.

**37** The words of the Lord, exalted and sanctified is He: “He is the One singing upon the branches.”

**38** We have sent down what lay concealed in the kingdom of utterance and made manifest what was stored in the Books of God, the Lord of the worlds. Among the people are those who have perceived the fragrance of utterance and turned toward the All-Merciful, and among them are those who have turned away and denied what has come from the heaven of grace, from God, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. Bliss be upon the one who has heard the call and been drawn by the verses of God, and perdition upon every heedless one who remains far away. Those who have tasted the sweetness of utterance are indeed numbered among the people of Baha in the Book of God, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.

**39** Khalil! The Wronged One remembers you from the prison and brings you glad tidings of your Lord’s loving favors, reminding you through His verses. He is indeed the All-Bountiful, the Generous. We have revealed for you and for those whose names have been brought before Our face that which makes them independent of the books of the world. To this bears witness this clear Tablet, revealed at this moment by the Pen of God, the Lord of the Day of Judgment. When you have drunk the wine of revelation from the cup of utterance and the attraction of the verses of your Lord, the All-Merciful, has taken hold of you,

**40** Say: “My God, my God! I testify to Your oneness and uniqueness, and to what has flowed from Your all-glorious Pen and descended from Your most exalted horizon. I ask You, O Desire of the world and Beloved of the nations, by Your Most Great Name, which You have made a light for those of Your servants who are near to You and those of Your creatures who are sincere, and a fire for those who have turned away from You and Your verses and opposed You in Your days, to strengthen this servant of Yours to tear through the veils of Your servants and the veils of glory of Your creatures. Enable him in all circumstances to do that through which the fragrance of Your good pleasure may spread. And I ask You, O Lord of all creation and Lord of the throne and the earth, to make me detached from all but You, steadfast in aiding Your Cause, and eloquent in that which draws Your servants near to the court of Your might and beauty. By Your beauty, O Dayspring of beauty, and Your majesty, O Dawning-Place of majesty! I cherish existence only to remember and praise You, and I desire only what You have ordained for me through the Pen of Your decree. My Lord! Strengthen me to do what befits Your days and Your revelation, and what You have sent down in Your Book.”

**41** I ask You, by the traces of Your Pen, the pervasive power of Your will, and the might of Your purpose, to strengthen Your servants to return to You, to turn in repentance at the door of Your grace, and to bow before the manifestations of Your grandeur. My Lord! Do not withhold them from the waves of the ocean of Your utterance or from beholding the signs of Your power in Your days. You are the One whom neither the affairs of the world nor the nations’ rejection can hinder. You are the One, my God, who brought forth Moses from Pharaoh’s house despite him and Your enemies, and delivered Abraham from a blazing fire, manifesting Your power and sovereignty. I ask You, by the verses of Your Cause and the banners of Your resolve, to ordain for Your loved ones the good of the next world and this world, and whatever will draw them near to You, O Possessor of all things. There is no God but You, the All-Powerful, the Omnipotent.” End.

**42** I ask and hope that God, glorified be His glory, will strengthen the gentleman mentioned—may the glory of God rest upon him—and enable him to serve the Cause with joy and delight, wisdom and utterance. Our Lord, the All-Merciful, is indeed powerful over whatever He wills, and He is the Compassionate, the Generous.

**43** The mention of Aqa Mirza ʿAbdu’llah Kh. A.—may the glory of God rest upon him—who has turned toward the Most Exalted Horizon through the guidance of the spiritual friend, his honor Huda—may the glory of God and His loving care rest upon him—was honored with a hearing in the presence of the Lord of Revelation. A most exalted, most holy Tablet was revealed especially for him and dispatched.

**44** The words of the Lord, exalted and sanctified be He: “He is the One who speaks in the Kingdom of Utterance.”

**45** A Book sent down by the Wronged One for whoever desires to drink the sealed wine from the hands of the bounty of his Lord, the All-Protecting, the Self-Subsisting, so that the call may draw him near to the Most Exalted Horizon and strengthen him in remembrance and praise. Blessed is the one who has heard and attained, and woe to every heedless one shut out by veils.

**46** We have heard mention of you. We remembered you before, and do so at this time, as a bounty from God, the Lord of the unseen and the seen. You have brought the servant who attends before Our face with a letter from one who has loved Me, held fast to My cord, soared in the heaven of My love, and arisen to aid My Cause among My servants; your name was in it. We have sent down from the heaven of grace verses that nothing whatsoever can equal, so that you may thank your Lord, the Possessor of existence.

**47** Beware lest the events of the world keep you from the Lord of eternity, or the doubts raised by the nations veil you from this sealed Cause. Say: “People of the world! The horizon of revelation has been illumined by the Lord of destiny, and what lay hidden in the Books of God, the Almighty, the All-Loving, has appeared. Set aside what you possess and take hold of what you have been commanded by the True One, the Knower of all hidden things.”

**48** We have turned from the most eloquent tongue to the luminous tongue. Today the world is illumined by the lights of revelation, and all things are occupied with remembrance and praise, joy and gladness. In the divine Books, earlier and later, the greatest rejoicing has been raised in commemoration of this blessed Day. Blessed is the soul who has attained and become aware of the station of this Day. Today the sound of the divine Pen is raised, and its horizon is manifest. Blessed is the soul whom the doubts and allusions of the people of the world have not kept from the Lord of eternity or deprived of the Most Great Ocean.

**49** Blessed are you and the one who brought you glad tidings and guided you to My straight path and My mighty Announcement. Thus have We enabled you to hear My sweetest call and sent you that which has delighted the eyes of those brought near.

**50** Here We also remember your wife, remind her through My verses, and give her glad tidings of My loving care and My mercy, which has preceded all who are in the heavens and on earth. May the glory shining from the horizon of the heaven of My loving care rest upon you, upon her, and upon those whom the armies of the Pharaohs and the ranks of tyrants have not frightened away from God, the Lord of the worlds. Praise be to God, the King, the True One, the Just, the Manifest.

**51** End. He has also been mentioned before. This transitory servant asks and hopes that God, exalted be His station, will assist him to arise wholeheartedly in service to His Cause and attain enduring stations in these fleeting days. He is the Powerful, the Mighty.

**52** I also convey greetings and salutations to his honor Hadi, that is, Huda—may the glory of God, the Most Exalted, rest upon him. Praise be to God, he is occupied with service and has received loving favor. We ask God, our Lord and your Lord, to place in his utterance that which will draw people toward His manifest horizon and His mighty Cause. Your mention of his honor Has Kh. A. and his honor Mirza Muhammad Kh. A.—may the glory of God rest upon them both—was likewise presented. A wondrous Tablet shone forth from the horizon of the heaven of grace especially for each of them and was dispatched, so that their eyes might be gladdened by them and they might thank their Lord, the Compassionate, the Generous. This servant also conveys greetings to them and asks God, glorified be His glory, to strengthen them. He is powerful over all things.

**53** Your mention of the friends in the land of Ya—may the glory of God rest upon them—was presented in the Most Holy Court. One by one, they were favored with the remembrance of God, glorified be His glory, and these verses shone from the horizon of His will. His words, glorified be His glory and all-embracing His bounty:

**54** “I am the One who hears and answers.”

**55** At this moment, when the One who spoke on Sinai is established upon the throne of revelation, the messenger of utterance has brought these words from the garden of meanings: “People of Baha! Adorn yourselves with the ornament of deeds and character, so that the horizons may be illumined by them. These are words We revealed in another Tablet and have recalled for you in this clear Book. Hear My call from the direction of My prison: there is no God but Me, the All-Powerful, the Omnipotent.”

**56** “I have manifested Myself and summoned the servants to the ocean of My grace. Some have turned toward Me and some have turned away. Blessed is the one who has turned toward Me and whom the rejection of the transgressors has not hindered. We remembered you before through My verses, and at this time through that which has enraptured the hearts of those who recognize Me. We have ordained that aid be rendered through the fear of God. Blessed is the one who holds fast to it; woe to the heedless. Aid your Lord, the All-Merciful, with the hosts of good character. This is what you have been commanded in various Tablets, and I am the Ordainer, the All-Wise. Take up the cups of salvation in the name of the One who causes the dawn to break, then drink from them in My mighty and wondrous remembrance. Say: ‘People of the world of being! The lights of utterance have encompassed you. Fear the All-Merciful and do not be among those who turn away. Turn toward God. What you see today will perish, and you will see yourselves among those who have suffered the greatest loss in the presence of God, the Almighty, the Most Great. Where are the kings of Persia and their sons, and the Pharaohs and their traces? Consider, then remember how, when Muhammad, the Messenger of God, came, you opposed Him and sought to extinguish His light. But God protected Him with the hosts of the unseen and the seen and exalted His Cause, O My loved ones in Ya Kayf. He is indeed powerful over whatever He wills and rules over whatever He desires. There is no God but Him, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.’”

**57** “My beloved ones! My loved ones! Thank God for enabling you to hear His call, showing you the traces of His Pen, and guiding you to His straight path. Blessed are you, and joy be yours, for attaining what the learned and the religious scholars of the earth have not attained. Preserve this most exalted station in the name of your Lord, who speaks in this lofty station. Thus has the Pen spoken as the Lord of eternity walks in His mighty prison. May the glory shining from the horizon of the heaven of My loving care rest upon you and upon whoever has turned toward God, the One, the All-Aware.” End.

**58** Praise be to God, all have been favored with the writings and illumined by the rays of the sun of utterance. I ask God to grant success to all and strengthen them in teaching the Cause, and I ask Him, exalted be He, to reinforce them with the hosts of utterance. He is indeed the All-Powerful, the Almighty, the One whose help is sought.

**59** Another letter from that beloved of the heart, from whose horizon the sun of unity shines, arrived and accomplished its work. Its mention was penetrating and \[corrupted original text\] pervasive. Praise be to God, its breeze brought joy and its fragrance spread a banquet of delight. After it was presented in the most exalted, most holy Court, this utterance descended from the divine Kingdom. The words of the Lord, exalted and sanctified be He:

**60** “In the name of Him through whom the gate of the Kingdom has been opened to kings and subjects.”

**61** “May the glory of God, His loving care, and His mercy rest upon you. At this moment I make mention of My own Self on your behalf, and We describe Him in terms befitting Me and worthy of a most holy Court, as a recompense for your deeds in My path and for your offering of your soul, your body, your tongue, and your pen in My remembrance, My praise, and service to My mighty and unassailable Cause. You have a treasure with God. He will pay your reward in full. He is your Guardian in the next world and this world, and He is the Compassionate, the Generous. May the glory shining from the horizon of the heaven of My mercy rest upon you, upon those with you, and upon those whom the affairs of the world have not kept from the Cause of his Lord, the All-Knowing.” End.

**62** Two verses have descended from the heaven of supreme loving care; truly, two worlds cannot equal them. May they bring you joy and delight! You mentioned the gathering of the friends of God at the home of Áqá Mírzá Sulaymán and Áqá Mírzá Mihdí—may the eternal glory of God rest upon them—who had been invited to a feast by Amín—may the all-glorious glory of God rest upon him. After these matters and the names of those assembled were presented in the most exalted, most holy, most inaccessible Court, these verses shone forth from the horizon of the heaven of the loving care of God, exalted be His glory.

**63** The words of the Lord, exalted and sanctified be He: “He is the One who remembers His friends with a remembrance that no other remembrance can equal.”

**64** A. Ḥ. The Wronged One has turned toward you from the prison and says: “Praise be to You, O God of the unseen and the seen, for enabling Your servant to turn toward You, to direct himself toward the lights of Your face, to look toward Your horizon, and to hold fast to Your cord. I ask You to strengthen him in steadfastness in Your Cause and to make his deeds a treasure for him in Your presence. Then forgive him through Your grace. You are indeed the Most Bountiful, the Generous.”

**65** O Nabíl before Bá! The Wronged One has remembered you in many Tablets and has sent down for you in these days that whose fragrance, were it to spread, would enrapture the hearts of those who recognize Him. Say: “Praise be to God, the Lord of the worlds.”

**66** J. V. You have attained My remembrance and the traces of My Pen. Recognize the worth of this most exalted station and say:

**67** “Praise be to You, O Lord of all creation, for enabling me to turn toward You and acknowledge what the Tongue of Your grandeur has spoken. I ask You to enable me to preserve what You have given me through Your bounty and generosity. You are indeed the All-Bountiful, the Generous.”

**68** O Abú Ṭálib! The One sought remembers you, and the Wronged One has turned toward you. Blessed is the seeker who has attained the One sought, the one endowed with recognition who has recognized its Object, and the one endowed with knowledge who has turned toward the One to be known. Take hold of the Book of God with strength from Him, despite those who have denied His testimony and His proof. Truly, in the eyes of the Concourse on high in this noble station, they are among those who have suffered the greatest loss.

**69** O Muḥammad ʿAlí! He who spoke on Sinai is established upon the throne of revelation. He has caused you to hear His call, sent down His verses for you, and sent you that which every learned scholar and every discerning knower is powerless to describe. O ʿAlí! The Wronged One remembers you in prison. Say: “O people of the world! Today the sun of this utterance shines resplendent from the horizon of the heaven of divine counsel: ‘Take My path; leave aside all paths other than Mine.’” Blessed is the soul who has attained a hearing and drunk from the cup of steadfastness. Thank God for remembering you. He remembers whoever loves Him. He is indeed the One who remembers, the All-Knowing.

**70** O Muḥammad before ʿAlí! You have attained the writings of the Most Exalted Pen. Praise be to God, you have torn through the veils of vain imaginings in the name of the Lord of humankind. Today the Most Great Balance is set before the eyes of the world and proclaims at the highest pitch: “I am indeed the All-Knowing Discerner.” Blessed is the one whom no power has hindered and no might has frightened, and who has turned toward the Most Exalted Horizon with supreme steadfastness. He is numbered among the people of Bahá in a manifest Tablet.

**71** O Riḍá! Blessed is the soul who today has attained the word of good pleasure. He is reckoned among the people of the Most Exalted Paradise. Delusive hopes have kept people from their ultimate end; for the sake of a few numbered days, they are deprived of and barred from the everlasting Kingdom. Leave them to their vain pursuits and say: “Praise be to You, O my God, for enabling me to turn toward You and causing me to voice Your beautiful praise. I ask You to ordain for me what will draw me near to You. You are indeed the All-Hearing, the Responsive.”

**72** O Ḥájí ʿAlí before Akbar (M. Y.)! You are remembered in the Most Great Scene and have received the loving care of God. Today the preface to the Book of Justice is adorned with this exalted utterance: “O people of the world! You are the drops of one sea and the leaves of one tree. Set aside dissension and discord; hold fast to unity and concord.” This is what you have been commanded by God, the Lord of the Day of Meeting. Yet the ears of the people of the world are deprived of hearing and barred from the exposition, for the reins of all have been and remain in the grasp of the ignorant, except those whom God wills. Blessed are you for recognizing the Desired One when those who associate partners with God denied Him.

**73** O ʿAlí-Akbar! Today the sun of remembrance shines resplendent from the horizon of the heaven of the Most Exalted Pen. The purpose is that souls should be educated under the shelter of the Cause and arise to extinguish the fire of hatred burning in the breasts of the diverse peoples of the world. May the eyes of the world behold such a day. Enmity has always been the cause of ruin, and unity the source of prosperity. Ask God that those who claim allegiance to the Most Exalted Horizon may attain true hearing and carry out what they are commanded to do. Blessed are you for hearing the call and answering your Lord.

**74** O Muḥammad Q.! Today the world has received and been illumined by the lights of the Most Great Remembrance, and the Wronged One has, with His loudest call, awakened His servants and shown them the way. Blessed are the souls who have attained the Day and recognized the Desired One. We ask God to strengthen everyone and not deprive them of the fragrant breezes of His verses.

**75** O Karbaláʾí Ṣádiq! The opponents among the people of the Bayán have denied the manifest Truth. Souls heedless of the Beginning and the End have arisen to harm the Cause and have seized upon every means in the hope of fulfilling their ambitions, which bring ruin in this world and the next. We ask God to make His friends so steadfast that the clamor of the world will neither hinder nor deprive them.

**76** O Muḥammad Mihdí! When the attraction of My call seizes you and you attain the choice wine of My utterance, say: “My God, my God! Increase the light of my sight that I may behold Your Most Exalted Horizon, and the strength of my hearing that I may hear the movement of Your All-Glorious Pen. O Lord! I am the one who has placed his trust in You and committed his affairs to You. Ordain for me the good of the next world and this world. There is no God but You, the Strong, the All-Powerful.”

**77** O Mihdí! The Guide came; they denied Him. The Truth came; they accused Him of falsehood. The ear given to falsehood cannot hear the call of Truth, nor is the idle eye fit to behold it. Praise be to God, the company of His friends has been endowed with keen sight. They are the souls of whom He says: “They were given insight by God.” They heard and saw and attained that which was the purpose of creation.

**78** O Varqá! My glory and My loving care rest upon you. These remembrances conclude with your remembrance. Blessed are you, and may bliss be yours! You are ever remembered in the Most Holy Court and receive the boundless favors of the Desired One of all peoples. Convey to ʿAzíz and Rúḥ a greeting of glory on behalf of God, and show them signs of affection and loving care and expressions of mercy on behalf of the Wronged One, that through God's loving care they may grow and bear fruit. He is indeed the Compassionate, the Generous, and He is the Ever-Forgiving, the Merciful. End.

**79** To God belong grace and bounty. Each star in the heaven of recognition has acquired radiance and is illumined and brightened by the lights of the Most Great Luminary. These remembrances and descriptions in truth reflect the limitations of souls; how could they be worthy of this station? Whatever has proceeded from this servant has never been, and is not, worthy of the court of God. To Him belong praise and acclaim, thanks and glory, for He imparted the stations and degrees of helplessness and nothingness and accepted them. No deed, no remembrance, and no thought, whether of the outward or the inward world, can equal this station.

**80** You mentioned the handmaids of God—may the glory of God rest upon them. After this was presented in His presence, each was adorned with the ornament of remembrance and received the favors of the kingdom of utterance. We ask our Lord, the Lord of earth and heaven, to ordain for them the good of the next world and this world. Glory be to God! The mystery of the Cause and its consummate wisdom are hidden from sight. A scholar who for years, as he imagined, sought knowledge in order to recognize the One to be known turned away from beholding Him when the lights of His face shone forth; yet the leaves and handmaids of God, who had not attended school and had outwardly acquired no share of learning, were illumined by the light of recognition and given to drink from the cup of steadfastness. Grace is indeed in His hand and in the grasp of His might. He gives and withholds, and He is the Almighty, the One who chooses.

**81** As for what you wrote concerning the person who was expected but later did not come because of ill health, and who expressed the hope that his name might be mentioned in the radiant Presence: he is Áqá ʿAlí Mílání—may the glory of God rest upon him. After this matter was presented before the face of the Lord of creation, these verses descended from the kingdom of the utterance of the All-Merciful.

**82** The words of the Lord, exalted and sanctified is He: O ʿAlī, you are remembered, and the Perspicuous Book turns toward you and speaks. You accepted what all have turned away from, and acknowledged what the people deny. You drank the choice wine of recognition on a day when the people of the world were deprived of it and veiled from it. Now consider what tongue is needed, and what utterance would be fitting, to offer adequate thanks.

**83** Say: Praise be to You, my God, and all bounty is Yours, O my Creator and my Hope. I testify that You have sent down Your blessing, sent forth the table, and made manifest the proof. I ask You, O Creator of the world, by the Most Great Name, to aid me in what will draw me near to You, so that neither the clamor of Your creatures may bar me from the court of nearness nor the doubts of Your servants keep me far from Your presence. O Lord, You see me holding fast to the cord of Your generosity. I ask You, by the lights of the sun of Your knowledge and the mysteries of Your Book, to ordain for me what will endure as long as Your kingdom and Your dominion endure. There is no God but You, the Bestower, the Munificent, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. End.

**84** You also mentioned the last gathering at the home of Jināb-i Khalīl—upon him be 9 66 \[the glory of God\]—and mentioned Jināb-i Āqā Mullā Muṣṭafā—may the glory of God rest upon him—and Jināb-i Āqā Mīrzā ʿIbād Allāh—upon him be 9 66 9 \[the glory of God\]. After this was presented, the Tongue of Grandeur spoke these radiant verses. His words, blessed and exalted is He:

**85** O Muṣṭafā, My glory rest upon you. The eternal, all-glorious Tree in the highest Paradise speaks this exalted word: “Blessed is the one who has recognized the station of the Day of his Lord and acted as befits it.” Praise be to God, you have heeded the divine call and turned toward the Most Exalted Horizon. Set your sights high. He is with you and aids you in remembering Him, praising Him, and serving His Cause.

**86** Say: My God, my God, I am Your servant, the son of Your servant and Your handmaid. I testify that You created my tongue to remember You, my sight to behold Your signs, my ear to heed Your call, my heart to recognize You, my hand to take hold of Your Book, and my foot to remain steadfast on Your path. O Lord, aid me in that through which the fragrance of Your good pleasure is diffused. This is better for me than all that is in the world to come and in this world. You are the Master of all creation and the Lord of the throne and the earth. There is no God but You, the Expounder, the All-Wise. End.

**87** And this is what was revealed for Jināb-i Āqā Mīrzā ʿIbād Allāh—upon him be 9 66 \[the glory of God\]. His words, blessed and exalted is He:

**88** He is the Witness, the All-Aware.

**89** God, glorious is His glory, sent a Herald and gave glad tidings so that the people of the earth might be adorned with joy and gladness and, with the utmost delight, approach His court. Yet because the hearts of His servants are occupied with vain imaginings, they have remained deprived of the lights of the morning of certainty, and these life-giving tidings have become a cause of sorrow, for their hearts are occupied with something else and their ears are accustomed to the harshest of voices. Glory be to God! Sweet, refreshing water flows before their faces, and the Most Great Luminary shines from the loftiest horizon of the world, yet the people are heedless. In every circumstance one must beseech God, glorious is His glory, not to deprive His servants. Praise the Desire of all the worlds, whose glad tidings bestowed life and who aided you to turn toward Him, approach Him, and recognize Him. He is indeed the Most Bountiful, the Generous. There is no God but Him, the All-Powerful, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. End.

**90** This transient servant, too, sends greetings to each one, offers an expression of God's greatness, and asks God to grant everyone that whose remembrance is lasting and enduring. You mentioned the spiritual friend, Jināb-i ʿ. B.—may the glory of God, the All-Glorious, rest upon him—and also the things he sent. Praise be to God, they arrived, and since they had been sent with pure intent, each attained its own station, and the friend who sent them has repeatedly been remembered in the Most Holy Court and in the gathering of those who circle around it. My beloved Jināb-i Amīn—may the glory of God rest upon him—was repeatedly mentioned, and the musk-willow water, which was truly the crown of the world's fragrances, was used in the most exalted, most holy Court and by the people of the pavilion of chastity and purity. My beloved Jināb-i Amīn—may the glory of God rest upon him—also did what was desired. This transient one longs to speak with a hundred thousand tongues in gratitude and praise to God, for He aided him, and he attained acceptance in the Most Holy Court. May God, glorious is His glory, protect His loved ones and enable them to attain the highest that is possible. He is indeed powerful over all things. Truly, that beloved of the heart is present before His face together with every one of those things. This is the word for which he had expressed his hope. Praise be to God, it was illumined with the light of an answer.

**91** You had mentioned Jināb-i Karbalāʾī ʿAbd al-Ṣamad—may the glory of God rest upon him—of M. R. This was presented in the most exalted, most holy Court, as was the prayer that had flowed from the tongue of the Desired One and which he had asked you to present on his behalf in the Most Holy Court. His request was fulfilled, for on one of the nights these details were presented and the prayer was also recited. This is what the Tongue of Grandeur spoke in reply:

**92** His words, exalted is His majesty: He is the Speaker in the kingdom of utterance.

**93** O Ṣamad, My glory rest upon you. You have been mentioned by one who loved Me, sought Me, held fast to My cord, clung to the hem of My robe, voiced My praise among My servants, and arose to aid My Cause. We have remembered you with verses which, were you to cast them upon a mountain, would cause you to hear it cry, “Here I am! Here I am, O Desire of the Concourse on high and Beloved of all who are in the heavens and the earths!” O Ṣamad, since you were present before the throne, heard with your own ear the call of your Lord, and saw with your own eyes the horizon of the Revelation of God, the Lord of the worlds:

**94** Say: My God, my God, praise be to You for enabling me to hear that for which You created me. You are the One, my God, who awakened me when I was asleep, raised me when I was seated, taught me when I was ignorant, drew me near when I was far away, gave me Your sealed choice wine to drink, and sheltered me in the refuge of Your name, the Self-Subsisting. I ask You, by the manifestations of Your power and the expressions of Your grandeur, to make me steadfast in Your Cause, constant in Your love, and firmly rooted in Your Word. You are indeed the All-Powerful, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. End.

**95** Truly, fresh bounty reached Jināb-i Ṣamad—upon him be 9 66 \[the glory of God\]—and the favor of the One came to his aid. Blessed is he, and whoever has attained the favor of his compassionate, generous Lord. Your other letter opened the door of joy and spread a banquet of delight. A hundred thousand blessings upon the joy and gladness that appear from the direction of the loved ones! That joy is the king of joys, and that gladness is the chief of the world's gladness and the light of the nations' delights. Glory be to God! The pen does not pause, and thought does not cease. I fear that so much writing may keep that beloved Ṣadr from his necessary tasks: transcribing the verses, making known the clear proofs, and reminding the servants. Praise be to God, you are assisted in remembrance, praise, and service. Evidence of this is your own statement, which you wrote: “What had been revealed in honor of the loved ones in this land—may the glory of God rest upon them—was recited on three occasions when, with due regard for wisdom, they gathered, and each, with his entire being, offered thanks and praise to the Desired One—glorious is His bounty and mighty His bestowal. As for what had been revealed in honor of the chosen ones in other lands, I copied and sent each item separately. I have also made a copy of the letter, still unfinished, to be sent to all the lands once completed, since in these days there is no one but this transient one engaged in transcribing”—and so on to the end of your statement. A hundred thousand joys cannot equal the joy this has brought, for through God's infinite bounties your sight, hearing, tongue, hand, pen, and ink are all engaged in service and intent upon exalting the Word. I ask and hope of God, glorious is His glory, that through the work of each of these members, the members of the world may arise to perform the deeds enjoined upon them and put them into practice.

**96** Regarding your mention of the treatise of proofs revealed by the Pen of God, it is evident that you perceive the fragrance of the utterance of the All-Merciful. The world's sense of smell is blocked, except for those whom our Lord, the Lord of earth and heaven, wills. He specifically summoned those four individuals to appear before the throne, but they did not succeed in doing so. One of those four was Jināb-i Āqā Mullā Muḥammad—may the glory of God rest upon him—who had been with those individuals for reasons of wisdom. The other three are outwardly counted among the people of the Qurʾān, but before the throne they have been associated with the tree of opposition. If the whole world were to listen free of ulterior motives, those few blessed pages alone would guide everyone and draw them to the Most Great Ocean. I ask God to purify all of selfish motives, so that they may become worthy to listen and capable of beholding.

**97** O God, my God, my Master, my Lord, and my Desire! Strengthen the heart of whoever desires to remember You and serve Your Cause, \[corrupted original text\] in the fluency of his tongue in praising You, his memory in reciting Your verses, and his foot in arising to enforce Your laws. You are indeed the Strong, the All-Powerful.

**98** As you appointed this servant to make the visitation on behalf of that beloved one and Jināb-i ʿAlī before Bā—may the all-glorious glory of God rest upon him—one night I set out for the most distant Goal, entered His presence, and attained the visitation. The Tongue of Grandeur pronounced the word of acceptance. May this bring joy to you, to him, and to this servant! Your other letter, whose opening spoke plainly and explicitly of separation from the Beloved of the worlds and conveyed the degrees of your longing, yearning, attraction, joy, and delight, aroused a sense of regret. I hope and ask of God, glorious is His glory, that He may graciously bestow these states upon this transient servant at all times. His are praise and bounty, for He has bestowed what has neither likeness nor equal. The mention of separation from that beloved one kindled the fire of love in the heart, while the longing for reunion and attainment to His presence brought forth the light of delight. Praise be to Him in every matter and every circumstance.

**99** Every letter betokens His loving care, and every word bears witness to His grace. You mentioned His Honor Ismu’llāh al-Jamāl—may the most glorious of all glory rest upon him—and whatever had flowed from his pen in remembrance and praise of God, glorious is His glory, was presented before the Most Great Ocean and received the honor of being heard. When it was finished, the Tongue of Grandeur spoke these resplendent verses in the kingdom of utterance. These are the words of the Lord, exalted and sanctified is He:

**100** “O Warqāʾ, you who drink My sealed wine, hold fast to My name, the Self-Subsisting, and uphold My irrevocable Cause! The ocean of loving care is now surging, and the sea of joy is manifest at the highest station of the contingent world, for the fragrance of the most great love rises and spreads from what was related of the submissiveness, humility, steadfastness, supplication, and entreaty expressed by My name Jamāl—upon him be My glory. O Jamāl! You expressed your powerlessness before the might of God, glorious is His glory. Now the All-Powerful makes mention of you, and the Almighty has turned toward you. You expressed your nothingness; the absolute Truth has turned toward you from the direction of the prison. In this station, your powerlessness is the pride of the powers of the people of the earth, and your nothingness is the crown of the existence of nations. He who soared in the atmosphere of My nearness, My love, and My loving care mentioned you and your words of remembrance and sent them to My prison. A servant attending Me presented them, and the Tongue of My Grandeur answered you. You asked for a sprinkling; My ocean has poured down upon you. You sought a drop; the rains of My mercy have showered upon you. Blessed is he who mentioned you! Reflect on nothingness and its station, for it has become the dawning-place of this most great loving care. Consider the expression of poverty and its fruits, for it has turned the kingdom of wealth toward you. From both your mention of your love for him who loved and his mention of you, a light shines in the worlds of love, affection, fellowship, and unity. May it bring joy and delight to you both! We ask God to illumine the horizons of the hearts of His loved ones with this light, so that all may hold fast to the most great cord of divine love. This is the Kawthar of life that flows and streams from the Pen of the All-Merciful. Glory be upon you both; mercy be upon you both; loving care be upon you both; grace be upon you both.”

**101** Here it ends. The station of concord and unity, especially among those souls counted as Hands of the Cause, is desired and beloved in the sight of God. Indeed, after the letter that His Honor Ismu’llāh—may the all-glorious glory of God rest upon him—had written to that beloved one was read, together with that beloved one’s mention of the letter, the Beloved’s lips smiled. What was revealed on this occasion is a trustworthy testimony and a manifest witness to the loftiness of the station of concord and unity before God, the Master of creation. This transient servant offers His Honor greetings and praise. I have continually asked the All-Sufficing, the Most Exalted, for whatever will bring about the elevation and exaltation of His loved ones. My Lord is indeed the All-Hearing, the Answerer.

**102** You mentioned the namesake of the Desired One, the son of Āqā Mīrzā Muḥsin the physician, who ascended to God—may the glory of God rest upon them both—and his brother, Jināb-i Āqā Mīrzā Jaʿfar—may the glory of God rest upon him. After this was presented before the throne, He spoke these words, the words of the Lord, exalted and sanctified is He:

**103** “Upon you be My glory and My loving care. We remember the son of him who attained My love, lived in My love, and ascended in My love. Convey greetings to him on behalf of the Wronged One and say: O namesake of the Desired One! Praise be to God, the luminary of grace has shone from the horizon of the heaven of bounty with a radiance that has encompassed the world. We ask God to confirm you in deeds from which everyone endowed with the sense of smell may inhale the fragrance of divine good pleasure. The door of grace is open, the throne of utterance is visible at the center of the contingent world, and the divine Preacher is seated upon it. By night and day He has called out in the loudest voice with verses that bring honor to existence and counsels that lead to exaltation, and has offered His exhortations. O Warqā! The dust of vain imaginings has enveloped some. Your Lord indeed knows the treachery of the eyes and what lies hidden in the hearts.”

**104** “We mention Mīrzā Jaʿfar as a token of grace from Us, and I am the Most Bountiful, the Generous.”

**105** “O Jaʿfar! Take what has been revealed in the Book and leave aside what the factions possess. Some deluded souls are occupied with leading others astray, some voice fabrications, and a group clings to vain imaginings and conjectures. God is sanctified beyond comprehension and recognition, and His Cause is more manifest than the sun. We ask God not to deprive hearing and sight, and not to withhold the Kawthar of utterance from those on earth. The loved ones of God must guide people through their character, conduct, and deeds, and show them the way to the Most Great Ocean.” Here it ends.

**106** Everyone endowed with sight, hearing, and a heart is bewildered as to what intoxication has seized the servants, that they neither distinguish nor discern between the sun and a glowworm. On one occasion, this exalted utterance shone from the dawning-place of the light of eternity. These are the words of the Lord, exalted and sanctified is He:

**107** “O servant in attendance! Even now it is not possible to speak of the manifest Truth. Despite the sound of the Most Exalted Pen and the call of the Master of Names, no true hearing or sight has been seen. He is deemed unworthy to be beheld and undeserving to be heard. Consider the people of the Bayān: although the error, waywardness, and loss of the Shīʿih community are plain and evident, they are once again engaged in forming such a community. By the life of God, that community has not perceived the fragrance of divine unity. They have been, and remain, worshippers of idols and vain imaginings. Until now, God has spoken with restraint, for the servants are weak. Over centuries and ages they have been brought up on vain imaginings. Inflamed eyes are unfit to behold the sun’s rays; deluded souls are incapable of receiving the effulgences of the luminary of certitude. Their beginning is conjecture, and their end is vain imaginings. Thus has spoken the tongue of \[corrupted original text\], the Almighty, the All-Knowing.” Here it ends. The mention of Jināb-i Āqā Sayyid Faraju’llāh—upon him be 9 66 \[the glory of God\]—flowed from that beloved one’s pen. After it was presented before the throne, the luminary of this utterance shone from the horizon of the heaven of proof:

**108** “O Faraj! Upon you be My glory. Your mention is remembered and your name recorded. We saw and heard, and spoke this utterance in the kingdom of proof. In these days your mention has repeatedly flowed from the Most Exalted Pen. Thank your Lord. Ask God to confirm you in remembrance, praise, and the promotion of the Cause. He indeed has power over all things. Convey greetings to the people of that land on behalf of the Wronged One, and remind them of what befits the days of God.” Here it ends.

**109** You also mentioned Jināb-i Āqā Mīrzā Āqā Sh—may the glory of God rest upon him. After this was presented, these verses were revealed. These are His words, blessed and exalted is He: “The gloating of enemies, the oppression of the wicked, and the afflictions of the world: We accepted and bore them all for the deliverance of the world. Yet all are heedless except those whom God wills. Praise your Lord for having confirmed you, taught you, granted you recognition, and given you to drink of the Kawthar of recognition from the hands of grace and bounty. We ask Him to enable you to remain steadfast in His irrevocable, firm Cause.” Here it ends.

**110** You mentioned Jināb-i Āqā Mīrzā Majīd’s journey in that direction—may the glory of God rest upon him—as well as his steadfastness and ardor. After this was presented in the Most Holy Court, these words were revealed. These are His words, blessed and exalted is He:

**111** O Majīd, delusions have seized the world, and causes of conflict and disorder are evident on every side. In this century, newspapers have gained prominence in the world, and their proprietors regard them as a means of building up the world, educating the nations, and advancing, refining, informing, and enlightening its people. They are, in truth, instruments of gathering and dissemination. “The day when the earth recounts its tidings” is seen and heard, and “the entire earth will be in His grasp on the Day of Resurrection” is plain and manifest. In secret, the earth has wondrous and sublime accounts to tell and speaks of tidings new and old; outwardly, too, the bird of news flies in every direction. Yet it is regrettable that some newspapers also publish fabricated reports without investigation. Whatever anyone says, they repeat, and whatever anyone writes, they reproduce. Thus, those who are the sources of delusions disseminate their imaginings through newspapers. O Majīd, reflect on “the day when the sky brings forth a manifest smoke.” In these days, falsehood flourishes greatly. The dust of delusions has kept the people from the Lord of Days. We ask God to raise up souls who will speak the truth and whom the barriers and opposition of the people will not deprive of the Day of Return. Blessed is anyone who has heard My call, arisen to serve Me and My loved ones, and voiced My beautiful praise. Praise be to God, the Unique, the One, the Almighty, the All-Beauteous. Here it ends.

**112** Indeed, newspapers sometimes traverse the earth, sometimes fly on the pinions of news, and sometimes change their name and become an electric current. From it, accounts, reports, and writings fly forth. Yet I beseech God, exalted be His glory, to assist their proprietors, so that all may act as is fitting. It was not expected that some European newspapers would make statements without investigation or follow the fabricated accounts of individuals. Day and night, the embodiments of delusion send letters to newspapers, and these are printed without investigation. Since some are eager for fresh news, they print them. I ask God to assist everyone to act according to His exalted words: “Do not believe every speaker, nor place your trust in every report that arrives.” Repeatedly, certain individuals in various places have wished that an account be written and sent so that they might publish it in books and newspapers. This was not accepted. To this day, no word has been given. The matter is in His hands. He does what He wills and ordains what He desires, and He is the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.

**113** You wrote concerning the two Riḍās. After this was presented, a most exalted, most holy Tablet was revealed from the heaven of divine favor specifically for Jināb-i Āqā Muḥammad-Riḍā Mīlānī—may the glory of God rest upon him—and was sent. He said: “This is better than permission, and I am the Most Bountiful, the Generous.” A most exalted, most holy Tablet was also revealed and sent specifically for Jināb-i Āqā Mīrzā Ḥasan—may the glory of God rest upon him—whom you mentioned. I ask God to enable him to preserve this supreme favor. He is indeed the Answerer.

**114** What you wrote concerning the son of the late Jināb-i Āqā Mīrzā ʿ. B.—may the glory of God rest upon him—was read. After it was presented in the Most Holy Court, He said: “A Tablet has been revealed concerning him. If it is appropriate, let them deliver it; otherwise, no.” That beloved one, however, must act with great wisdom, for if one offers counsel or advice to people of that kind, those very words become a cause of hatred and disorder.

**115** What was mentioned at the end of this letter concerning humility, submissiveness, supplication, and prayer to God, exalted be His glory, attained the honor of being heard. These are His words, blessed and exalted is He: “We have heard from you what befits the court of My might and the throne of My grandeur. Blessed is your tongue, for it spoke words from which the fragrance of My favor, My bounty, and My mercy spread; and blessed is your eye for what it witnessed and saw, and your ear for having heard the call of God, the Speaker, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. Your turning toward Me, your presence, your devotion, and your supplication have been accepted in the days of God, the Lord of the worlds. We ask God to aid and confirm you in spreading His Cause, exalting His Word, and disseminating His laws. He has power over all things.” Here it ends.

**116** After that beloved one’s prayer and expressions of humility and supplication were presented, the Euphrates of mercy flowed and the sun of loving-kindness shone from the horizon of the heaven of bounty. The ocean of the All-Merciful’s utterance surged to such a degree that this evanescent servant is powerless and unable to describe it. We ask, through the wonders of His bounty, that He bestow a sprinkling of this grace upon the people of the world, so that all may attain what brings everlasting existence and eternal life.

**117** In that beloved one’s other letter, after expressions of remembrance and praise and ascent to the heaven of recognition of the Lord of Names, you mentioned the spiritual friend Jināb-i Nūrī—may the glory of God, the All-Glorious, rest upon him—and also set down the passages he had mentioned. After this was presented in His presence, the Tongue of Grandeur spoke these verses. These are His words, blessed and exalted is He:

**118** “ʿ. B., you have always been and remain remembered. His remembrance taught you to remember Him. His loving-kindness took you by the hand. His mercy showed you the way, and His bounty encompassed you. He granted knowledge, bestowed insight, gave assistance, and lent support. Praise be to God, you have attained what has never had and has no equal. You have been mentioned in all the letters of Varqā—upon him be My glory and My loving-kindness. We ask Him, exalted is He, to aid and confirm you in what He loves and approves, and to ordain for you what will be a light before your face in every one of His worlds. He has power over all things.” Here it ends.

**119** News of him and of his health and well-being has arrived repeatedly from the Land of Ṭā. The friends in that land have often spoken well of him. In truth, he speaks the truth and is engaged in service. You mentioned your honored brother, Āqā Mīrzā Ḥusayn—may the glory of God rest upon him. After this was presented in the Most Holy Court, these verses were revealed from the kingdom of the All-Merciful’s utterance:

**120** The words of the Lord, exalted and sanctified is He: “O Ḥusayn, upon you be My glory. God willing, may you attain what is fitting and be among the fruitful saplings whose growth becomes manifest in the divine days. God has planted new saplings with the hand of loving-kindness and watered them with the water of His favor, that they may bear fruit and give shade. Blessed is anyone who attains this most exalted station. Say: ‘O God of Names, praise be to You for having honored me, enabled me to see, and enabled me to hear. I ask You to confirm me in what You love and approve. You are the Lord of all creation and the Lord of the world to come and of this world.’” Here it ends.

**121** This servant also conveys greetings and praise to him and asks God to grant him success and support. Concerning what you wrote about Jināb-i Ustād Ḥusayn—upon him be 9 66 \[the glory of God\]—that he has newly reached the water’s edge of recognition: after the mention of him attained the hearing of the Lord of all creation, the luminary of bounty shone from the horizon of the kingdom of utterance, and these verses were revealed. These are His words, exalted be His glory and all-embracing His bounty:

**122** “Praise God for having enabled you to turn toward Him on a day when smoke has enveloped the inhabitants of the earth, and for having taught you when the people were in manifest ignorance. Say: ‘Yours is the glory, O Lord of Names, and Yours is the loving-kindness, O Lord of creation, for having enabled me to recognize the ocean of Your utterance and the heaven of Your bounty, and for having illumined me with the rays of the sun of Your revelation. O Lord, confirm me in steadfastness in Your Cause, and enable me to remember and praise You. You are the All-Powerful, the Almighty, the Omnipotent, and worthy to answer prayers.’” Here it ends.

**123** And these pearl-like words were revealed from the dawning-place of the will of the Lord of Names and Attributes specifically for the two sons of Jināb-i Mullā Muṣṭafā and Āqā Ghulām-Ḥusayn—may the glory of God rest upon them. The words of the Lord, exalted and sanctified is He:

**124** “O children of humanity, strive to manifest what befits the divine days. This Wronged One counsels you to do what will bring exaltation and elevation.
