Adorn your persons with the ornament of deeds and your heads with the crown of good character, so that the world may be illumined by them both. The light is manifest and shining, and the luminary of the Cause is visible and radiant. Demons—that is, heedless souls—have always lain and still lie in wait for human beings. Protect yourselves through the name of God. Be aware; be watchful. This is His counsel. Blessed are those who act upon it.” Here it ends.

**125** Thanks be to the Desire of the world. His loving-kindness embraces everyone. The spring rain of His mercy has always fallen ceaselessly upon the soil of hearts. His generosity has encompassed existence, and His bounty has bestowed what has had neither equal nor likeness. Yet that beloved of the heart and this servant must ask God, exalted be His glory, to rend the obstructing veils, that perhaps they may see and recognize. Concerning your mention of the exalted lady, the mother of the two dear ones, Jināb-i Āqā Mīrzā Sulaymān and Jināb-i Āqā Mīrzā Mahdī—may the glory of God rest upon her and upon them both—after this was presented in His presence, these exalted words were revealed and made manifest from the dawning-place of the will of God, exalted be His glory. These are His words, exalted be His utterance and exalted His proof:

**126** “O Pen, remember the leaf who left her homeland, turning toward the Most Exalted Horizon, to appear before the Countenance, stand at the door, hear the call of the Wronged One, and behold the horizon of Revelation. I testify that she heard the call of her Lord, believed in Him, turned toward Him, and bore witness to that to which the Tongue of Grandeur bore witness. Blessed are you, My handmaiden and My leaf! You attained My remembrance before your ascension and after it. Blessed are you for having attained the days of God and His writings on a day when the women of the earth and its queens turned away. We perceived from you the fragrance of love for Me and of turning toward the lights of My face. We ask God, exalted be He, to admit you into the highest Paradise, adorn you with the crown adorned with His All-Glorious name, and send down upon you at every moment mercy from Himself and light from His presence. He is indeed the All-Powerful, the Ever-Forgiving, the Generous. Glory from Us rest upon you and upon the handmaidens who remember you through what the Most Exalted Pen has uttered on this dark night.” Here it ends.

**127** Truly, these are days when, reflecting from one perspective, a person longs for death, since after ascending one attains the writings of the Most Exalted Pen; yet from another perspective, one longs to remain alive, in the hope of rendering some service. The truth, however, is that whatever the Beloved has willed is what is beloved. Peace is the best conclusion. He said specifically: “We console Jināb-i Mīrzā Sulaymān and Mīrzā Mahdī—My glory rest upon them both—and remember them with words that will open the gates of joy and transform sorrow into the greatest happiness. At the time of her ascension, there was revealed concerning her from the Most Exalted Pen that which is abiding and everlasting.” Here it ends.

**128** Previously, too, there was revealed from the Most Exalted Pen concerning the aforementioned lady that whose fragrance will endure as long as the earthly realm and the Kingdom endure. Blessed is she! What you mentioned concerning Jināb-i Āqā Mīrzā Maḥmūd of Marāghih—may the glory of God rest upon him—was granted, and this evanescent servant, acting on your behalf and his, attained His presence at a specially appointed time and was adorned with acceptance. I ask Him, exalted be He, to make the drop of my deed an ocean from Himself. He is powerful over all things. You also mentioned Jināb-i Āqā Mīrzā Mahdī Shaffāfī—upon him be 9 66 \[the glory of God\]—and requested special favor for him. After this was presented, the Tongue of Grandeur uttered these verses. The words of the Lord, exalted and sanctified be He:

**129** “In My name, the Wronged One, the Stranger.”

**130** “God, exalted be His glory, is at all times occupied with remembering His friends. The Tongue of Grandeur speaks and His Pen moves. By the life of God, nothing visible or manifest can equal the writings of His Pen. O Mahdī, thank your Lord for this exalted utterance. When you sense the fragrances of the All-Merciful’s words, say:

**131** ‘My God, my God! I testify that You created me to know You, to turn toward the lights of Your face, to direct myself toward the horizon of Your Revelation, to stand at the gate of Your grandeur, and to appear in the court of Your glory. I ask You, by Your greatest signs, by the manifestations of Your power in the earthly realm of creation, by the ocean of Your grace and the heaven of Your knowledge, to make me steadfast in Your Cause and a herald of Your name. O Lord, ordain with the Pen of Your generosity for this servant of Yours what will draw him near to You in every world among Your worlds. Then ordain for him what You have ordained for Your servants who have not broken Your covenant and pledge, and who, in Your days, have drunk the choice wine of revelation from the hands of Your bounty. You are indeed the All-Powerful, the All-Protecting, the Almighty, the All-Wise.’” Here it ends.

**132** And your handwritten letter, beloved of the heart, which was sent in the name of the honored friend, Jināb-i Alif and Ḥā—may the glory of God and His loving-kindness rest upon him—attained the honor of being heard by the Desire of all worlds. His words, blessed and exalted be He:

**133** “Praise be to God, who has aided Alif and Ḥā to turn toward Him, hold fast to the cord of His grace, cling to the hem of His mercy, and arise to serve His Cause. He is indeed the Compassionate, the Helper, the Ever-Forgiving, the Generous. O Varqā, My glory and loving-kindness rest upon you. The Most Exalted Pen testifies to his turning toward God, his devotion, and his service. In days when the limbs of existence trembled at the might and tyranny of the people of the earth, he turned toward God, attained the knowledge of Him, spoke His remembrance, and acknowledged and professed His Word. Blessed is he, and bliss be his! Give him glad tidings on My behalf and remind him of what has been sent down from My Pen, that he may rejoice and be among the thankful.” Here it ends.

**134** The spiritually beloved Jināb-i Amīn—may the glory of God rest upon him—acted in accordance with his wishes. He has repeatedly mentioned him, his sons, Āqā Mīr ʿAlī Akbar, and Āqā Mīr ʿAlī Aṣghar—may the glory of God rest upon them—and has likewise mentioned all the other friends among the people of Mīm and Yā and Sīsān. In most of his letters, he has also mentioned you. I ask God to aid him under all circumstances in loving His friends. He is indeed the Helper, the All-Powerful, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

**135** Another leaf, which grew from the tree of love for the Beloved of all worlds, arrived in the form and shape of a letter. Praise be to that pen and inkwell from which spiritual water flows! When that water, flowing from the spring of love, reached the soil of the pages, flowers of singular sincerity, humility, reverence, remembrance, and praise sprang forth. A hundred thousand praises to that pen, that inkwell, and that letter! After inhaling the fragrance of the flowers and acquainting myself with the writings, I proceeded to the most glorious, most exalted station, and the letter attained the honor of being heard.

**136** The words of the Lord, exalted and sanctified be He: “In the name of Him through whom the Tablet was borne and the Pen set in motion.”

**137** “My glory, My loving-kindness, and My mercy rest upon you. The servant is present with the letter; the call of the tongue of the heart has attained the honor of being heard. We have heard and seen. Blessed is your heart, for it has turned toward My luminous horizon; and its tongue, for it has voiced My beautiful praise; and its face, for it has been illumined by the lights of the Countenance; and its essence, for it has gained its being through love for Me, the Almighty, the Inaccessible. O Varqā, the loving-kindness of God and His mercy rest upon you. The days of your presence are ever remembered in this court. In your early days you arose to serve My Cause, guide My servants to My path, refine souls through My verses, and purify them with the water of My loving-kindness that flowed from the clouds of the heaven of My will. Blessed are you, and bliss be yours and his who loves you for the sake of God, your Lord and the Lord of all worlds. Glory rest upon you and upon those who are with you.” Here it ends.

**138** Praise and thanks be to Him, for on this blessed night special loving-kindness has encompassed you, and you have been adorned with a special distinction. God willing, may you be aided and enabled to educate His servants, refine souls, and attract hearts and inmost beings. After the prayer was presented before the Countenance, the Most Great Ocean surged with a wave that this servant is powerless to describe. At the end, the Tongue of Grandeur uttered these blessed words: “Varqā—My glory and loving-kindness rest upon him—turned toward Us with the face of his heart, the tongue of his heart, the heart of his heart, and the essence of his heart. He has been set ablaze with the fire of love for your Lord and has attained the heavenly stream of His remembrance, the All-Attracting, the Most Bountiful, the Quickener, the Giver of Life, the Mover, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.” Then it concluded with these blessed words. He said: “Blessed is he!”

**139** Regarding the matter in question, what took place was correct and acceptable. Indeed, people such as these should not be discouraged, nor should their desires be followed. A middle course should be maintained. It is surprising that even Jināb-i Letter Sīn has not yet understood the purpose, although he attained the Most Great Prison twice and on each occasion resided nearby for a time. I ask God, exalted be His glory, and hope that He will acquaint him with the purpose. On one occasion He said: “Ask God to aid him in that which will bring about his protection and salvation. When seeking closeness in the service of kings exceeds its bounds, there is a danger of harm.” Here it ends.

**140** This evanescent servant asks God to aid Ḥaḍrat-i Muʿīn in exalting the Word and spreading the Cause. If he turns his attention to this station, divine assistance and the mercy of the All-Merciful will assuredly aid him and bestow what is fitting. You had mentioned the honored gentleman, Jināb-i Mīrzā F. Ḍ.—upon him be 9 66 \[the glory of God\]. Some time ago, a most exalted, most holy Tablet was revealed from the heaven of grace especially for him and was sent. From every letter of that blessed Tablet waft the fragrances of everlasting loving-kindness. Praise be to God, he is aided in steadfastness, service, remembrance, and praise. I convey to him greetings, praise, magnification, and glory. God willing, the effects of his excellence will become manifest and evident throughout the regions and lands at the command of the All-Powerful, the Unconstrained.

**141** All those present and those who circle around convey greetings of glorification, send their salutations, and offer praise. Regarding the matter in question, one should act according to the previously cited tradition transmitted by the Shiʿa, which states: “Neither compulsion nor delegation, but a matter between the two.” Glory be to God! To this day, these gentlemen have not understood the loving-kindness, compassion, and mercy of God, exalted be His glory, although all the Tablets bear witness and testify to it. This servant asks his Lord to help them recognize what He has intended. He is indeed the All-Hearing, the Responsive.

**142** Mention of that solace of the eyes named Valīyuʾllāh—upon him be the glory of God—was presented at the Most Holy Court. These resplendent verses were revealed especially for that solace of the eyes and the other cherished children—may God’s protection and loving-kindness rest upon them. These are the words of the Lord, exalted and sanctified is He:

**143** He is the One who speaks in the kingdom of utterance.

**144** Blessed are you for having turned, in your earliest days, toward your Lord, the Lord of the mighty throne. Say: “My God, my God! You see me turning toward the heaven of Your revelation, voicing Your praise and Your verses, and acknowledging what has shone from the horizon of the kingdom of Your recognition. I ask You to aid me in championing Your Cause and exalting Your Word, so that the banners of Your Cause may be raised in Your cities and Your lands. You are indeed the Lord of the world and the Educator of the nations. There is no God but You, the Strong, the All-Powerful.”

**145** And this is what was revealed for ʿAzīzuʾllāh—upon him be the glory of God:

**146** In My name, shining from the horizon of the heaven of proof.

**147** The Wronged One has heard your call and answered you with that which is a gentle rain of mercy for the good and blessed lands, a breeze of loving-kindness for the gardens of knowledge, a sun of certitude for the heaven of utterance, a river of life for the thirsty, and the fragrance of the All-Merciful for the people of Bahāʾ. Give thanks to My Most Exalted Pen: it has indeed made mention of you in words that will endure as long as the kingdom of God, the Lord of the worlds.

**148** This is what was revealed for Rūḥuʾllāh—upon him be the glory of God:

**149** In the name of Him who is hidden even while He is manifest and evident.

**150** What the tongue of your heart uttered attained the honor of being heard. Say: “My God, my God! Praise be to You for having created me through Your most exalted Word and brought me into being in Your days, O Lord of all creation and Lord of the throne and the earth. I ask You, by the Ark upon which the Most Great Ocean has established itself, and by Your Cause through which You have subdued the world, to let me dwell beneath the shelter of the domes of Your mercy and the heaven of Your grace. Then ordain for me what will draw me nearer to You in every circumstance and aid me in championing Your Cause. You are indeed the Self-Sufficient, the Most Exalted. There is no God but You, the Almighty, the All-Bountiful.” Here it ends. Praise be to God.

**151** The cherished children have received the favors of the Desire of all the worlds. For each of them, an enduring blessing and a spiritual feast have descended from the heaven of grace. May it bring them joy! As their names were presented, He smiled, and the ocean of loving-kindness rose in a wondrous wave to a mighty height. His are all praise and glorification, and His are all thanksgiving and glory. At that time, the newborn—upon him be the glory of God, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy—who is adorned with the name Badīʿuʾllāh, was honored with approval. May bliss be his! This servant asks God and hopes that He will strengthen each one with the aid that is clear and evident in the revealed verses. “O Warqāʾ, upon you be My glory and My loving-kindness.” Praise be to God, you yourself have attained this supreme distinction and are adorned with this most great gift. “To this testify the tongue of My grandeur, the tongue of My grace, the tongue of My loving-kindness, and the tongue of My wondrous utterance.” Here it ends.

**152** This is yet another grace, another blessing, another mercy, and another gift from God, our Lord and the Lord of all who are in the heavens and the earth.

**153** What you wrote concerning Jināb-i Āqā Mīrzā Āqā Sh.—upon him be the glory of God—his wish to turn toward the lights of the Beloved’s countenance, and his burning in the fire of separation, attained the hearing of Him for whose call ears were created to listen. This is what the Tongue of Grandeur uttered in reply. These are the words of the Lord, exalted and sanctified is He:

**154** He is the Witness, the All-Aware.

**155** We have heard your call and seen your turning toward Us, your devotion, and your burning in separation from your Lord. We have previously made mention of you in words through which the breeze of the All-Merciful has wafted throughout existence. We ask God to aid you and enable you to remember and praise Him and to serve His Cause. He is indeed the All-Powerful, the All-Protecting, the Self-Subsisting. When you have drunk the choice wine of revelation from the cup of My utterance and perceived the fragrance of the All-Merciful from My words,

**156** say: “My God, my God! Separation from You has brought me to ruin, and distance from You has consumed me. Your revelation has bewildered me, Your verses have set me aflame, and Your clear proofs have drawn me to You. I ask You, by the Word through which those who are near to You hastened to the place of sacrifice, to inscribe for me, with Your Most Exalted Pen, the reward of meeting You, of being present before Your face, and of standing at the door of Your grandeur. O Lord, You see me enraptured by the breezes of Your revelation and soaring in the atmosphere of Your love. I ask You, by the rains of the dawn of Your revelation and the lights of Your countenance, to enable me in every circumstance to hold fast to the cord of Your grace and to act according to what You have commanded me in Your Book. You indeed have power over whatever You will. There is no God but You, the Strong, the All-Powerful.”

**157** God has loved and continues to love His loved ones, and has come so that they may meet Him and witness the manifestations of His loving-kindness and mercy. But the oppression of the oppressors and the heedlessness of the heedless have intervened. For some time, the land of the prison has been seen to be in turmoil, for a person from among the people of hatred occupied the seat of government for a while. Although he returned to hell—that is, he was dismissed—the land has not yet become calm. We have therefore refrained from uttering the word of permission. He is indeed the All-Bountiful, the Generous, and He is the Ever-Forgiving, the Merciful. We ask Him for that in which lies the good of this world and the next. He indeed has power over all things and is worthy to answer prayers. Here it ends.

**158** Praise be to God, he has attained what has never had, and does not have, any likeness or equal. The details of events in this land have surely reached your hearing by now. This servant also conveys greetings of glorification to him and asks God, exalted be His glory, to grant him the good of this world and the next. Regarding what you wrote again concerning Jināb-i Ḥājī Muḥammad ʿAlī—upon him be 9 66 \[the glory of God\]—on the day the letter from you, that beloved friend, arrived, what he desired was presented at the Most Holy Court and received the honor of approval. May it bring him joy! Jināb-i Amīn, the beloved of the heart—upon him be the glory of God—also presented his requests at the Most Holy Court and heard the approval with his own ears. Likewise, a Tablet had previously been revealed especially for him and sent. This servant asks his Lord to aid His loved ones in what He loves and approves, and to ordain for them the best of what has been revealed in His lucid Book.

**159** And regarding what you wrote concerning divinity, that someone had become distressed on hearing it mentioned, after this matter was presented, these exalted words appeared from the dayspring of the Will and

**160** shone forth. His words, blessed and exalted is He: “O Warqāʾ, upon you be My glory and My loving-kindness. People are weak. To this day, the Most Exalted Pen has not spoken as is befitting. Although His verses have encompassed the world, He who spoke on Sinai regards Himself as silent, and the ignorance of the people of the Qurʾān has not yet been fully described. By the life of God, they are deprived of the cup of divine unity and barred from the chalice of singleness. To this day, the station of true divine unity remains concealed. This concealment is a great favor to some of the souls who have turned toward Him, although the fragrance of this station wafts from the Most Exalted Pen. The point is that few ears are found ready to hear the call of God, and few eyes keen enough to behold what has appeared from the treasuries of the Pen. You should show forbearance and speak of things that will cause people to turn toward Him, embrace His Cause, and be attracted to Him. For if some aspects of the ranks and stations of the holy ones of the Qurʾān, and of the degrees of what is fitting for this Revelation, remain concealed, this is nearer to piety. For now, love and acceptance suffice. After accepting and turning toward Him, most ascend by the cord of utterance and become acquainted with these degrees according to their capacity. We have ordained abundant good for you in the Book.” Here it ends.

**161** O beloved of my heart, most are nursing infants: they seek milk and have never been, nor are they now, capable of taking anything beyond it. We ask God, exalted is He, to aid His servants in remembering and praising Him, turning toward Him, and placing their trust in Him. He is indeed the All-Hearing, the Responsive, and He is the Unique, the One, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.

**162** Replies have been revealed to the petitions sent to the Most Holy Court. I ask God that all the friends in that land may be illumined by the radiance of the light of the Sun of Truth shining from the horizon of the Tablet, become ablaze with the wondrous, exalted fire, and arise in unity and concord. May they devote themselves to the betterment of the world with radiant hearts purified of rancor and hatred, so that the light of concord may encompass the world and the enmities concealed in human hearts may subside and disappear.

**163** It is hoped that the people of Bahā—may the soul of the world be sacrificed for them—will firmly brace themselves for action and rid the world of corruption, conflict, contention, and bloodshed, so that this hapless world may breathe a sigh of relief. I say this, but I hear, “Far from it, far from it!” For some souls have treated the Cause of God lightly. They play and do not understand, and say things of which they have no awareness.

**164** In all circumstances, this mortal servant seeks assistance and asks for success. Our Lord, the All-Merciful, is indeed the Compassionate, the Generous, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

**165** As for the matter of the two kinds of script, His Holiness the Greater Branch of God—may my soul and my being be sacrificed for the dust beneath His feet—has written concerning it. It is very good. He Himself will write out the details. Regarding your statement that one of the friends has asked about backbiting, these matters are as manifest and clear as the sun in the divine Tablets. In these days, all should be ablaze with the fire of the Word and engaged in service to the Cause. They should seize the opportunity the time affords and, through wisdom and utterance, awaken the people of the world. Every soul who today succeeds in acknowledging what God has sent down in the Book is named and counted among the inhabitants of the highest Paradise.

**166** Today is the lord of days, and the Lord of Revelations is established upon the throne of utterance. Blessed are those who have attained! In one sense, the days of the Manifestations of God are called the Day of God, but in all the Books these days are specifically associated with the revelation of the hidden Unseen and the treasured Mystery, who speaks with the loudest call before the faces of the world. The greatness of these days is mentioned and recorded in the former Books and in the Qurʾān.

**167** The Herald, namely the Primal Point—may the soul of all besides Him be sacrificed for Him—attained the honor of meeting, outwardly concealed from everyone, during the days of His journey toward Mākū. And Quddūs—upon him be My glory and My loving care—attained repeatedly. During the journey to the land of Khā, We expressly summoned him, and for several months he was in Our presence and attained the meeting. The Point—may the soul of all besides Him be sacrificed for Him—named him and the Most Great Bāb the First and the Last, and also referred to them as the first to arrive and the last to alight. He gave each of them the glad tidings of this Revelation, and specifically told Sayyāḥ—upon him be My glory—“Go; perhaps you will find.”

**168** The universal Manifestations were aware before their appearance. They are the dawning places of divine knowledge. We ask God to assist His friends in recognizing what He has sent down in His firm and lucid Book. Certain discussions cause veiling and also extinguish the fire of the divine Lote-Tree within one’s being. Glory rest upon whoever confines his gaze to turning toward the Most Exalted Horizon, detached from conjectures and vain imaginings. O beloved of my heart, certain discussions truly cause heedlessness and listlessness, especially the mention of what God does not approve. It is hoped that all will drink of the choice wine of the All-Merciful’s utterance and appear in the gathering of the world adorned with distinction. The people of God must assuredly be distinguished from others. Greetings of praise and peace have been and continue to be conveyed to the friends in that land, and this mortal servant asks and hopes that the abiding God will assist everyone to do what is fitting.

**169** Regarding the matter in question, it is very clear and evident that, in God’s sight, anything that harms someone or brings affliction upon a soul—indeed, anything that causes people sorrow and distress—is rejected and unacceptable in this Most Great Revelation. Whatever brings advancement, elevation, and exaltation, and causes joy and gladness in the hearts of the people of the world, is acceptable and beloved. Yet, in the interests of wisdom, one should act in such a way that no hint of despair arises. Our Lord, the All-Merciful, has forbidden everyone corruption and conflict and commanded them to show love, compassion, and affection. Wisdom, however, has always required and still requires forbearance. I ask God to assist the person mentioned in protecting the flock. In that case, divine assistance will assuredly reach him. He protects whoever turns toward Him, ordains for him the good of the next world and of this one, exalts him through His bounty, His mercy, and His sovereignty, and aids him with the hosts of the unseen and the seen. He is indeed the All-Powerful, the Omnipotent.

**170** As for the prayers, they were sent down from the heaven of loving care and dispatched in accordance with the request of the honored beloved, Mīrzā F. Ḍ.—upon him be the glory of God—as were the reply to the spiritual friend, Āqā Mīrzā Jalīl—upon him be 9 66 \[the glory of God\]—and those to the other friends—upon them be the glory of God. May that beloved of my heart deliver them to their recipients after reading and acquainting himself with them. As prayers specifically for sleeping and waking were requested, after the request was presented before the Throne, these radiant prayers shone forth from the horizon of divine utterance. His words—exalted be His grandeur and great be His power:

**171** You are the One who remembers, and You are the One remembered.

**172** O my God, my Lord, and my Desire! Your servant wishes to sleep in the shelter of Your mercy and rest beneath the domes of Your grace, seeking the aid of Your protection and Your watchful care. O Lord, I ask You by Your eye that never sleeps to guard my eye from looking toward anything but You. Then increase its light, that it may behold Your signs and gaze toward the horizon of Your Revelation. You are the One before the revelations of whose power the very essence of power has grown weak. There is no God but You, the Strong, the All-Conquering, who chooses as He wills.

**173** You are God; there is no God but You.

**174** Praise be to You, O my God, for awakening me after my sleep, bringing me forth after my absence, and raising me after my slumber. I have entered the morning turning toward the lights of the dawn of Your Revelation, through which the horizons of the heavens of Your power and grandeur have been illumined, acknowledging Your signs, assured of Your Book, and holding fast to Your cord.

**175** I ask You, by the might of Your will and the compelling power of Your purpose, to make what You showed me in my sleep the firmest foundation for establishing Your love in the hearts of Your friends and the best means for the revelation of Your grace and loving care. O Lord, ordain for me through Your Most Exalted Pen the good of the next world and of this one. I bear witness that the reins of all affairs are in Your grasp; You change them as You will. There is no God but You, the Strong, the Faithful. You are the One who, by Your command, changes abasement into glory, weakness into strength, helplessness into power, agitation into tranquillity, and doubt into certainty. There is no God but You, the Almighty, the Bestower. Do not disappoint whoever has asked of You, nor withhold from whoever has sought You. Ordain what befits the heaven of Your bounty and the ocean of Your generosity. You are indeed the All-Powerful, the Omnipotent.

**176** He is the Guardian over all names.

**177** My God, my God! How can I choose sleep when the eyes of those who long for You remain wakeful in separation from You? How can I rest upon my bed when the hearts of Your lovers are troubled by their estrangement from You? O Lord, I have entrusted my soul and my being to the right hand of Your might and Your protection. Through Your power I lay my head upon my bed, and through Your will and purpose I raise it from there. You are indeed the Preserver, the Watchful Guardian, the All-Powerful, the Omnipotent.

**178** By Your glory, I desire from sleep or wakefulness only what You desire. I am Your servant and am in Your grasp. Assist me to do that through which the fragrance of Your good pleasure may spread. This is my hope and the hope of those brought near to You. Praise be to You, O God of the worlds.

**179** He is the Hearer, the Responsive.

**180** O my God, I have entered the morning in Your shelter, and whoever has sought Your shelter should be under the care of Your protection and within the stronghold of Your defense. O Lord, illumine my inner being with the lights of the dawn of Your Revelation, just as You have illumined my outer being with the light of the morning of Your bounty.

**181** He is the All-Protecting, the Self-Subsisting.

**182** I have entered the morning, O my God, through Your grace, and I leave the house trusting in You and committing my affairs to You. Send down upon me from the heaven of Your mercy a blessing from Your presence. Then return me to the house in safety, just as You bring me out of it safe and steadfast.

**183** There is no God but You, the Unique, the One, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. Here it ends.

**184** The sun of divine grace has always been radiant and resplendent. He Himself is His proof, and the manifestations of His loving care are His signs. He is the Proof, the Manifest, the Witness, and the Expounder. His loving care embraces all, and His mercy encompasses everything. There has never been, nor is there now, any need for argument.

**185** You wrote concerning the honorable Ḥājī ʿAlī ʿAskar M. Y.—upon him be 9 66 \[the glory of God\]. After the matter was presented at the Most Holy Court, permission to return was sent down. Since he has a family, he must certainly act in accordance with the Most Holy Book. A hundred thousand blessings upon those who act accordingly! As for the fact that

**186** You wrote concerning the prisoner in Tiflis, Mashhadī Ismāʿīl the cord-maker. The matter was presented in His presence, and he received divine loving care and compassion. His name was mentioned by the Tongue of Grandeur, and He said: “Write to him: Do not grieve. The Lord of the world is in the Most Great Prison. Say: My God, my God! I have placed my trust in You and committed my affairs to You. Ordain for me what will benefit me in every world among Your worlds. You are indeed the All-Knowing, the All-Aware.” Here it ends.

**187** You mentioned the honorable Āqā Muḥammad Ṣādiq, who emigrated and attained His presence. A most exalted, most holy Tablet was sent down from the heaven of the divine will especially for him and dispatched. God willing, may he receive it and drink from the ocean of meanings. This servant also conveys greetings and praise of God to him and prays for his success.

**188** You wrote concerning that through which mercy for the world is manifested, and likewise His wrath—that is, ink, through which the vessels of the world sail and the pillars of nations are made firm. In truth, if all the pens of the world wished to count the offspring of this mother, they would find themselves powerless. Thought cannot encompass it, nor can volumes suffice for it. In short, even if its description were recorded on every sheet of paper, it would truly be as nothing before its lofty, all-subduing powers. In short, what has been described in these terms, and in terms beyond them, is very good and desirable. Thus \[it is\] mercy that is manifested through it.

**189** Glory be to You, O God of all contingent beings and Desire of all created things! You are the One who placed within a drop of a dark substance that which \[corrupted original text\] the people of the graves. Through it You gave life, and through it You seized and took away. I ask You, by Your power that holds sway over the world, to enable the nations to accept Your Cause. You are indeed powerful over whatever You will, and You are the All-Protecting, the Self-Subsisting. I ask You, O my God, by the ocean of Your loving care and the heaven of Your grace, to send down upon whoever has loved You and mentioned Your servant glory from You, peace from Your presence, and spirit from Your side. You are indeed the All-Powerful, whom nothing You witness and see can hinder, and You are the Lord of all creation and the Lord of the throne and the earth. There is no God but You, the Most High, the All-Glorious.
